name: Project Management Professional (PMP)®
title: PMP Exam Preparation
lead: Everything you need to prepare for the PMP exam in one place: what the exam covers, a study approach that works, five free full-length simulators with 900 original questions, and the guides to go with them.
heroAlt: Candidate taking a computer-based exam with project charts floating around the workstation

facts.text: domains: People, Process and Business Environment
free practice questions in five full PMPORT mocks

outline.name: People
outline.items: Leading teams, managing conflict, engaging and aligning stakeholders, communication and knowledge transfer.

outline.name: Process
outline.items: Planning and integration, scope, value delivery, resources, procurement, finance, quality, schedule, status and closure.

outline.name: Business Environment
outline.items: Governance, compliance, change control, impediments, risk, continuous improvement, organizational change and external changes.

audience: Project managers who lead and direct projects and want the most widely recognized project management certification.
eligibility: PMI requires project leadership experience (typically 36 months with a four-year degree, or 60 months with a secondary diploma) and 35 contact hours of project management education. Always check PMI's current PMP handbook before applying.
format: Scenario-based questions across predictive, agile and hybrid approaches
Multiple choice, multiple response, matching, hotspot and graphic-based items
Case studies that test how you apply judgement in context

plan.title: Weeks 1–2: Learn the outline
plan.text: Read the exam content outline and the PMBOK® Guide principles. Take one simulator in practice mode to find your weak domains.

plan.title: Weeks 3–4: Build the mindset
plan.text: Study the PMP mindset: servant leadership, value, collaboration and tailoring. Drill the People domain by task.

plan.title: Weeks 5–6: Process and agile
plan.text: Work through planning, schedule, cost, risk and agile practices. Practise the project maths with the calculators.

plan.title: Weeks 7–8: Full mocks
plan.text: Take full timed mocks, review every wrong answer and aim for a consistent 75% or more before booking the exam.

related.label: Free PMP study guide and 8-week plan
Best free PMP practice exams compared

faq.q: How hard is the PMP exam?
faq.a: It is demanding because questions test judgement in realistic situations, not memorization. Regular full-length practice is the best preparation.

faq.q: Are the PMPORT questions real exam questions?
faq.a: No. They are original practice questions written to the public exam content outline. Real exam questions are confidential.

name: Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM)®
title: CAPM Exam Preparation
lead: Start your project management career with the CAPM. Learn what the exam covers, follow a simple study plan and practise with five free full-length CAPM simulators: 750 original questions on fundamentals, predictive and agile delivery, and business analysis.
heroAlt: A new project team member studying a project life cycle, a Kanban board and a requirements map on a large screen

facts.text: minutes, with a 10-minute break after question 75
free practice questions in five full PMPORT mocks

outline.name: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts
outline.items: Life cycles and processes, planning, roles and responsibilities, following planned strategies, and problem-solving tools.

outline.name: Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies
outline.items: When to use a predictive approach, the project schedule, and documenting project controls.

outline.name: Agile Frameworks/Methodologies
outline.items: When to use an adaptive approach, iteration planning, adaptive controls, adaptive plans and task management.

outline.name: Business Analysis Frameworks
outline.items: BA roles, stakeholder communication, gathering requirements, product roadmaps, methodology influence and validating requirements.

audience: Students, career changers and team members who want to show they understand project management fundamentals before they lead projects.
eligibility: PMI requires a secondary degree and 23 hours of project management education completed before the exam. No project experience is needed. Check PMI's current CAPM handbook before applying.
format: Multiple choice, drag-and-drop matching, hotspot and short scenario items
Questions on predictive and adaptive approaches in all four domains
One optional 10-minute break; you cannot return to the first half after it

plan.title: Week 1: The basics
plan.text: Learn life cycles, process groups, roles and the project management plan. Take a practice set to see where you stand.

plan.title: Week 2: Predictive planning
plan.text: Study scope, WBS, schedules, critical path, baselines and change control. Practise schedule questions.

plan.title: Week 3: Agile
plan.text: Learn Scrum roles and events, Kanban, XP, backlogs, velocity and burndown charts.

plan.title: Week 4: Business analysis
plan.text: Study elicitation, requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, traceability and product roadmaps.

plan.title: Weeks 5–6: Full mocks
plan.text: Take full timed CAPM mocks, review explanations and repeat until you score 75% or more consistently.

related.label: Free project templates in Artifacts Lab

faq.q: Should I take the CAPM or the PMP?
faq.a: The CAPM suits people early in their career with little project experience. The PMP requires several years of project leadership experience.

faq.q: Does the CAPM include business analysis?
faq.a: Yes. Business analysis frameworks are 27% of the exam, so study requirements, stakeholders and roadmaps as well as project management.

name: Entry Certificate in Business Analysis (ECBA)™
title: ECBA Exam Preparation
lead: Begin your business analysis career with the ECBA. Learn how the exam is structured, follow a short study plan and practise with five free full-length ECBA simulators: 250 original questions across the nine knowledge areas of the current blueprint.
heroAlt: A new business analyst mapping a need, stakeholders and a solution around the six core concepts of business analysis

facts.text: knowledge areas in the current blueprint
free practice questions in five full PMPORT mocks

outline.name: Understanding Business Analysis
outline.items: What business analysis is, the BA role, key terms, requirement types and the core concept model.

outline.name: Mindset for Effective Business Analysis
outline.items: Curiosity, systems thinking, adaptability, ethics and collaboration.

outline.name: Implementing Business Analysis
outline.items: Planning and tailoring business analysis work and governance.

outline.name: Change, Need, Solution, Stakeholder, Value and Context
outline.items: The six core concepts applied to everyday situations: defining needs, comparing solutions, engaging stakeholders and assessing value in context.

audience: Students, graduates and career changers starting out in business analysis, and team members who want a recognized foundation.
eligibility: No business analysis work experience is required. You must accept IIBA's code of conduct and terms. Check IIBA's current ECBA handbook for any training requirements before applying.
format: Based on The Business Analysis Standard and the BABOK® Guide

plan.title: Week 1: Foundations
plan.text: Learn what business analysis is, requirement types and the six core concepts. Take a practice set.

plan.title: Week 2: Mindset and planning
plan.text: Study curiosity, systems thinking, ethics and how business analysis work is planned and governed.

plan.title: Week 3: The core concepts in practice
plan.text: Work through need, solution, stakeholder, value, change and context with real examples and techniques.

plan.title: Week 4: Full mocks
plan.text: Take full timed mocks, review every explanation and aim for 75% or more before booking.

related.label: DataLab: SQL, Excel and Power BI practice
Using Claude in PM and business analysis

faq.q: Do I need experience for the ECBA?
faq.a: No business analysis work experience is required, which makes the ECBA a good first certification.

faq.q: What changed in the ECBA blueprint?
faq.a: The current blueprint uses nine knowledge areas: three foundations from The Business Analysis Standard and the six core concepts applied in practice.

name: Certified Business Analysis Professional (CBAP)®
title: CBAP Exam Preparation
lead: Prepare for the CBAP with confidence. See how the exam is weighted, follow a study plan built around the BABOK® Guide and practise with five free full-length CBAP simulators: 600 original scenario and case-study questions.
heroAlt: A senior business analyst reviewing a case study with requirements models, a traceability matrix and a value analysis

facts.text: free practice questions in five full PMPORT mocks

outline.name: Requirements Analysis and Design Definition
outline.items: Specify and model requirements, verify, validate, define requirements architecture and design options, and recommend a solution.

outline.name: Strategy Analysis
outline.items: Analyse the current state, define the future state, assess risks and define the change strategy.

outline.name: Requirements Life Cycle Management
outline.items: Trace, maintain, prioritize, assess changes to and approve requirements.

outline.name: Business Analysis Planning and Monitoring
outline.items: Plan the approach, stakeholder engagement, governance, information management and performance improvements.

outline.name: Solution Evaluation
outline.items: Measure and analyse performance, assess solution and enterprise limitations, and recommend actions to increase value.

outline.name: Elicitation and Collaboration
outline.items: Prepare for and conduct elicitation, confirm results, communicate information and manage collaboration.

audience: Experienced business analysts who lead complex analysis work and want the senior IIBA certification.
eligibility: IIBA requires 7,500 hours of business analysis work experience in the last 10 years (with at least 900 hours in four of the six knowledge areas), 35 hours of professional development in the last four years, and two references. Check IIBA's current CBAP handbook before applying.
format: Scenario-based multiple-choice questions with one best answer
Case studies of several paragraphs followed by questions
Based on the BABOK® Guide v3, all 30 tasks

plan.title: Weeks 1–2: Map the BABOK® Guide
plan.text: Learn the six knowledge areas, their tasks, inputs and outputs, and the core concept model. Take a practice set.

plan.title: Weeks 3–4: RADD and strategy
plan.text: Focus on the biggest areas: requirements analysis and design definition, then strategy analysis.

plan.title: Weeks 5–6: Life cycle, planning, evaluation
plan.text: Study traceability, prioritization, change, governance and solution evaluation with scenarios.

plan.title: Week 7: Techniques
plan.text: Review the most-used techniques and when each one fits a situation.

plan.title: Week 8: Full mocks
plan.text: Take full timed mocks, review every case study and aim for 75% or more before booking.

related.label: DataLab: SQL, Excel and Power BI practice
Free BA templates in Artifacts Lab
Using Claude in PM and business analysis

faq.q: How is the CBAP different from the ECBA?
faq.a: The ECBA tests foundations and needs no experience. The CBAP tests how an experienced analyst applies the BABOK® Guide in complex scenarios and case studies.
Requirements Analysis and Design Definition is 30% of the exam, about twice any other area.

name: ITIL® Foundation (Version 5)
title: ITIL 5 Foundation Exam Preparation
lead: Get ready for ITIL® Foundation (Version 5). See what the syllabus covers, follow a two-week study plan and practise with five free full-length simulators: 200 original questions weighted like the real exam.
heroAlt: A service management team looking at a digital service lifecycle, value streams and an AI assistant on a service dashboard

facts.text: free practice questions in five full PMPORT mocks

outline.name: ITIL value system
outline.items: The seven guiding principles, governance, practices, continual improvement, and how opportunity and demand become value.

outline.name: Key ITIL terms and definitions
outline.items: Products, services and offerings; value, outcomes, costs and risks; utility and warranty; service relationships and roles.

outline.name: Four dimensions of product and service management
outline.items: Organizations and people, information and technology, partners and suppliers, value streams and processes, and external factors.

outline.name: Product and service lifecycle
outline.items: Discover, design, acquire, build, transition, operate, deliver and support, used iteratively.

outline.name: Value streams
outline.items: Identifying, mapping and managing value streams.

outline.name: ITIL and AI; ITIL and other frameworks
outline.items: Using AI responsibly in service management, and combining ITIL with Agile, DevOps and PRINCE2.

audience: Anyone who works in or with IT and digital services: service desk, operations, development, project and product roles.
eligibility: There are no formal prerequisites for the Foundation exam. Training with an accredited provider is optional. Check PeopleCert's current exam details before booking.
format: 40 multiple-choice questions with one correct answer
Standard, missing-word, list and occasional negative questions

plan.title: Days 1–4: Key terms
plan.text: Learn the definitions of service, product, value, outcome, output, cost, risk, utility and warranty, and the consumer roles.

plan.title: Days 5–8: Value system
plan.text: Study the seven guiding principles in depth, governance, the continual improvement model and key practice purposes.

plan.title: Days 9–11: Dimensions and lifecycle
plan.text: Learn the four dimensions, external factors, the eight lifecycle activities and value streams.

plan.title: Days 12–14: Full mocks
plan.text: Take full timed mocks and review every answer until you score 75% or more consistently.

faq.q: Is ITIL 5 very different from ITIL 4?
faq.a: Version 5 keeps the guiding principles and value system, adds the product and service lifecycle, and gives more attention to AI and to working with other frameworks.

faq.q: What score do I need to pass?
faq.a: The pass mark is 26 out of 40 (65%). Aim higher in practice to give yourself a margin.
